A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, framework, and substantial retained content. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original experiments on synthetic and real datasets, including robustness–consistency trade-offs, prediction-error analyses, and baseline comparisons.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original experimental results, including revised baseline comparisons and an added actionability/post-processing study.

M1.justification: The robust solver survives as v2 Algorithm 4, and the beta-weighted variant already existed in v1 Appendix B.2. The written coordinate procedure nevertheless changes: v2 Algorithms 1–2 explicitly restrict reversal of previous updates and terminate at zero update, whereas v1's loop terminated after a non-sign-flipping update. These are refinements to the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic, German Credit, Small Business Administration, and ACSIncome-CA data; the larger ACS experiment is retained, not newly added. v2 Appendix D.4 adds an evaluated German Credit scenario with immutable features removed and categorical feasibility constraints, which v1 only discussed.

E2.justification: v1 Figure 1 compares against ROAR's robust endpoint. v2 evaluates a prediction-aware, beta-dependent ROAR variant across the trade-off and adds it to the smoothness comparison in Appendix D.5/Figure 9. This substantially strengthens comparator participation in the learning-augmented experiments. RBR is retained in Appendix D.6.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 replaces validity under a single adversarial model found by projected gradient ascent with future validity under a model trained on shifted data. v2 also adds lambda = 0.3 to the sweep and introduces feature-filtering/projection protocols in Appendix D.4. The retained ACS figure still says worst-case validity, leaving its relationship to the revised protocol unclear.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.4/Figure 8 tests how actionability restrictions and categorical projection affect the robustness–consistency trade-off. Appendix D.5/Figure 9 extends prediction-error analysis with comparative ROAR behavior across predictions and beta values. The existing alpha-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both report averages over five folds and instances requiring recourse, with robustness and consistency error-bar plots in Figures 4–5. v2 retains the same described uncertainty construction; no new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence-interval methods, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 2 reports changed smoothness curves, Figure 1 adds ROAR trajectories, and v2 adds actionability and per-recourse runtime results. Figures 3 and 10 report future-validity outcomes replacing v1 Figure 3's worst-case-validity comparison, including strong RBR results on synthetic data. These are revised or newly reported outcomes, not uniform same-setting improvements. The ACS results are retained.

T1.justification: The main counterexample, lemmas, and optimality proof are retained in Appendix C, formerly Appendix A. v2 corrects the sign-function definition from an indicator to −1/0/1 and supplies the explicit infinity-norm neighborhood missing from v1's incomplete sentence. Theorem 3.3 and its introduction explicitly connect the beta endpoints to the retained optimization problems.

C1.justification: The learning-augmented framework and first-optimal-robust-solver claims remain central. v2 foregrounds Pareto dominance over prediction-aware ROAR across robustness and consistency. Its cost-validity summary is more qualified than v1's generally lower cost at fixed validity, emphasizing higher validity often without much higher cost.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of post-processing losses, explains ROAR's difficulty attaining optimal consistency through nondifferentiability, and suggests performativity as a prediction source. It removes v1's explanations attributing neural-network validity patterns to imperfect adversarial-model optimization after changing the evaluation. Most existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds per-recourse timings for Algorithm 1, ROAR, and RBR, baseline pseudocode in Appendix B, and concrete feature-filtering/projection instructions. v1's explicit grid-search description is no longer given. Hardware, model-training details, and Table 1's parameter values are retained.

R1.justification: The relocated related work is substantially expanded with recent recourse research, adversarial-training guarantees, and robust optimization. Appendix A more precisely positions ROAR as sharing the robustness framework, distinguishes RBR's data-shift objective, and explains why related robust-learning guarantees do not directly address this setting.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively condensed and rewritten. Detailed related work moves to Appendix A, the main proof sketch gives way to unified algorithm exposition, and the beta-weighted formulation moves forward from the appendix. Terminology changes from total cost to price, alongside substantial heading and paragraph revisions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces isolated ROAR points with full trajectories and changes legends and axis ranges. Validity plots are relabeled and replotted, and new actionability and paired algorithm/ROAR smoothness displays are added. The RBR comparison receives a separate appendix figure; existing error-bar, sensitivity, and ACS displays are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds informative prediction-aware baseline comparisons and an empirical actionability check. However, its new Algorithm 2 stores positive objective improvements but selects their minimum while claiming to choose the greatest improvement, leaving the reported procedure inconsistent. The revised future-validity evaluation also retains conflicting worst-case-validity descriptions in Appendix D.6 and unclear linkage to D.7. These benefits and unresolved methodological inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
